key_insight: Vision foundation models contain complementary information at different input resolutions — combining low-resolution global cues with high-resolution local detail at inference unlocks stronger, more robust representations than the standard single-scale approach.
problem_solved: Current practice restricts inference to a single input scale, losing complementary inductive biases learned at other resolutions and limiting performance, robustness, and transferability.
method: Enable multi-scale inference by routing or fusing features extracted at multiple input resolutions while keeping the base VFM weights unchanged.
Use lightweight scale-conditional modules or efficient feature-aggregation operators to combine global (low-res) and local (high-res) cues without large compute or retraining costs.
Design an inference-time strategy (e.g., selective fusion or ensembled predictions) that balances accuracy, robustness, and compute budget.
impact: Practitioners can extract more task-relevant information from pretrained VFMs without full model retraining, improving downstream accuracy and robustness with modest extra compute. This makes VFMs more adaptable across tasks and resource constraints.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing parallel low-res and high-res inputs into a shared VFM, followed by a lightweight fusion module and final prediction head.
Side-by-side feature-map visualization illustrating complementary global vs. local activations at different scales.
Bar chart comparing single-scale vs. multi-scale inference on accuracy and robustness metrics (no numbers required — relative bars).
Tradeoff plot of compute (latency or FLOPs) vs. performance showing Pareto improvements from the multi-scale strategy.
paper_title: MuRF: Unlocking the Multi-Scale Potential of Vision Foundation Models
paper_authors: Bocheng Zou, Mu Cai, Mark Stanley, Dingfu Lu, Yong Jae Lee
